device: Meta Quest 3 and 3S, current Quest Browser; flat page only (the XR session is M11b1). Records the signals, the backend and the adapter

steps.instruction: In Quest Browser open <preview>/?perf=1. The HUD must show a flat tier (the XR-capable provisional tier is mobile-low) and the backend. Expected backend: webgl2 (the xr-quest policy forces WebGL2). Write the backend and the HUD tier in notes.json observations.

Tap Export. In notes.json check signals.hasNavigatorXr (true), signals.immersiveVrSupported (true), signals.hasXrGpuBinding and signals.adapter (note vendor, architecture, description). If Export does not download in the headset browser, copy the output of JSON.stringify(__dvBridge.platform.signals()) from the remote DevTools console (chrome://inspect on the Mac).

Copy 'signals' from notes.json into tools/ci/fixtures/ua/quest-browser.json (set synthetic to false, keep the expect block: class quest, headset quest, provisional tier mobile-low). Run pnpm check:unit -- packages/shared: the fixture must still pass AC-2.
Tap 'Run 10 min' on the HUD and leave the browser window in view for 10 minutes (flat page, not an XR session).
Tap Export; save to docs/device-spike/M01c/quest3/. Record in the report: backend actually selected, adapter summary (navigator.gpu present or not on this browser), UA string, rafHz (72 or 90).
